problem: Clustering functional data is challenging when temporal misalignment obscures intrinsic shape differences, and existing methods treat registration and clustering as separate tasks.
approach: NeuralFLoC uses Neural ODE-driven diffeomorphic flows and spectral clustering to jointly learn smooth warping functions and cluster-specific templates in an end-to-end unsupervised framework.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art joint registration and clustering on functional benchmarks while establishing universal approximation guarantees and asymptotic consistency.

problem: Predicting dynamic ionic transport properties from static atomic structures is challenging because molecular dynamics simulations are computationally prohibitive and sequential inference methods suffer from error accumulation.
approach: Uses a non-autoregressive learning framework with auxiliary modality learning that treats atomic trajectories as an auxiliary input during training but does not require them at inference.
contribution: Achieves 200x speedup over autoregressive models while substantially reducing prediction error and benefiting from both trajectory and non-trajectory datasets.

problem: Non-stationary time series forecasting fails because models rely on static historical assumptions and become blind to evolving global context (phase amnesia).
approach: PULSE is a physics-informed framework using phase-anchored disentanglement, a phase router for trajectory generation, and Statistic-Aware Mixup to handle distribution shifts.
contribution: A simple MLP backbone achieves state-of-the-art performance on 12 real-world non-stationary forecasting benchmarks.

problem: Fine-tuning pre-trained diffusion and flow models lacks mechanisms to shape tail behavior, which is critical for controlling reliability (lower tail) and discovery (upper tail).
approach: Tail-aware Flow Fine-Tuning (TFFT) uses Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) with a decomposition into lightweight threshold optimization and entropy-regularized fine-tuning.
contribution: Enables efficient tail-aware distributional fine-tuning comparable in cost to standard fine-tuning while controlling worst-case and discovering high-reward samples.

problem: Traditional e-commerce search uses fragmented multi-stage cascading architectures with conflicting optimization objectives, limiting performance.
approach: OneSearch is an end-to-end generative framework with keyword-enhanced quantization encoding, multi-view user behavior sequence injection, and preference-aware reward-weighted ranking.
contribution: Achieves +1.67% item CTR, +2.40% buyer, and +3.22% order volume improvements with 75.40% operational cost reduction and increased Model FLOPs Utilization.

problem: Existing contrastive steering methods for LLM jailbreaking rely on limited biased prompts and require manual tuning of steering strength, limiting effectiveness and robustness.
approach: Adaptive steering uses model extraction to guide steering vectors toward ideal ones and adapts steering strength based on contrastive activation statistics.
contribution: Notably improves jailbreaking effectiveness and robustness without manual tuning, raising harmfulness score from 6% to 70%.

problem: Mechanistic interpretability of machine translation in LLMs has been limited to word-level analysis due to scale challenges.
approach: Analyzes attention heads across three model families and 20 translation directions to decompose translation into target language identification and sentence equivalence subtasks.
contribution: Finds distinct sparse attention heads specialize in each subtask; modifying 1% of heads enables instruction-free performance comparable to instruction-based prompting.

problem: Graph neural network simulators for CFD suffer from limited information propagation because classical GNNs only exchange information between neighboring nodes.
approach: Flow Alignment Rewiring (FLARE) connects 2-hop nodes only when their relative direction aligns with the input flow direction, informed by fluid physics principles.
contribution: Outperforms PIORF and other 2-hop rewiring methods significantly on flows over cylinders and airfoils under different conditions.

problem: Quality of environment and reward model fundamentally limits reinforcement learning effectiveness, but these components are typically optimized independently.
approach: RLAnything dynamically optimizes policy, reward model, and environment through closed-loop feedback with consistency feedback and critic-based environment adaptation.
contribution: Achieves 8.5% improvement on OSWorld with Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking and 21.2% and 12.1% improvements on AlfWorld and LiveBench.

problem: Preference learning for diffusion model alignment suffers from training instability caused by high gradient variances at different timesteps and off-policy bias.
approach: SIPO introduces gradient clipping and masking of uninformative timesteps plus timestep-aware importance reweighting to correct off-policy bias.
contribution: Achieves stabilized training across SD1.5, SDXL, and video models (CogVideoX, Wan2.1) with consistent improvements over existing alignment methods.

problem: Using AI-generated annotations for causal inference is challenging because naively pooling AI and human data induces bias, and existing methods assume AI outputs are label surrogates.
approach: Generative Augmented Inference (GAI) treats AI outputs as high-dimensional informative features for learning human labels using nonparametric methods.
contribution: Enables consistent estimation with valid inference from combined human and AI data, improving asymptotic efficiency and confidence interval quality.

problem: Autoregressive Metropolis-Hastings sampling for test-time scaling is inherently serial, limits GPU utilization, and exhibits extreme tail latency at high budgets.
approach: Adaptive Sequential Monte Carlo (ASMC) uses parallel particle inference targeting power-shaped trajectory distributions with cache coherent resampling that reorders KV caches.
contribution: Achieves 80.6% exact-match accuracy on MATH500 with p95 latency of 73.7s versus 1318s for sequential MCMC, providing efficient high-accuracy test-time scaling.

problem: LoRA fine-tuning is highly sensitive to hyperparameter choices and exhaustive hyperparameter search is computationally expensive.
approach: Uses Bayesian Optimization with a pre-trained LLM as a discrete-to-continuous mapping module guided by natural language prompts describing hyperparameter relationships.
contribution: Discovers hyperparameters achieving 20% performance improvement over standard choices using only about 30 iterations versus 45,000 combinations.

problem: Large language models fail at determining convexity of symbolic expressions under deep functional composition, exhibiting a compositional reasoning gap.
approach: ConvexBench benchmark uses an agentic divide-and-conquer framework with external parsing via Abstract Syntax Trees and recursive reasoning enforcement.
contribution: Achieves F1=1.0 at depth 100 versus 0.2 for standard approaches by addressing parsing failure and lazy reasoning failure modes.

problem: Vision-language-action models struggle with precise low-level actions from high-dimensional observations and bridging domain gaps across heterogeneous robot data sources.
approach: XR-1 learns Unified Vision-Motion Codes (UVMC) via dual-branch VQ-VAE jointly encoding visual dynamics and robotic motion, then applies three-stage training.
contribution: Enables scalable VLA learning across diverse robots, tasks, and environments with complementary multi-modal knowledge from heterogeneous datasets.

problem: Test-time scaling for complex reasoning through sampling is limited by verification: identifying correct solutions among candidates via scalar scoring is ineffective.
approach: V1 unifies generation and verification through pairwise ranking with V1-Infer using uncertainty-guided tournament-based ranking and V1-PairRL jointly training generator and verifier.
contribution: Improves Pass@1 by up to 10% on code generation and benchmarks while outperforming best-of-n and providing more efficient test-time scaling.

problem: Standard transformers cannot recognize context-free languages (CFLs) which formalize syntax in natural language and code, remaining a theoretical gap.
approach: Proves looped transformers with O(log N) layers and O(N^6) padding can recognize all CFLs, and unambiguous CFLs require only O(N^3) padding.
contribution: Establishes theoretical understanding of CFL recognition by transformers with empirical validation showing looped-padded transformers outperform fixed-depth on CFLs.

problem: Large language models memorize sensitive training data creating privacy and copyright risks, and existing unlearning methods often cause catastrophic utility loss.
approach: Divergence Decoding uses small auxiliary models to steer LLM logits away from specific data during inference via standard pre-training and fine-tuning.
contribution: Decisively outperforms state-of-the-art unlearning baselines and can be distilled back into the base model while generalizing to image domain.

problem: Cross-domain class-incremental learning suffers from entanglement between what to update and how to update, causing unstable adaptation and severe forgetting.
approach: Parameter-Masked Decoupled Optimization (PMDO) disentangles domain-relevant parameter adaptation from stability-aware trajectory regulation using domain-aware knowledge decoupling.
contribution: Enables effective cross-domain adaptation while mitigating catastrophic forgetting and maintaining long-term learnability across benchmarks.

problem: Efficient attention mechanisms like linear and hybrid attention lack rigorous theoretical characterization of expressive power relative to full attention.
approach: Theoretically characterizes expressive power hierarchy showing hybrid networks interleaving full and linear attention require 2^(3L^2) layers to match L+1 full attention layers.
contribution: Provides first provable separation between hybrid attention and standard full attention, establishing theoretical perspective on attention mechanism capabilities.

problem: LLMs for recommendations lack predictable scaling laws because raw user interaction data contains inherent noise, bias, and incompleteness.
approach: Creates layered framework generating high-quality synthetic pedagogical curriculum data for continual pre-training, demonstrating robust power-law scaling.
contribution: Synthetic data models outperform real data models by 130% on recall@100; establishes first robust power-law scaling for continual pre-trained LLMs in recommendations.

problem: Data assimilation with diffusion surrogate models lacks a method to integrate observations that guarantees sampling from the true posterior.
approach: SURGE performs Sequential Monte Carlo over diffusion trajectories using particle filtering with importance weighting and resampling on the path measure.
contribution: Provides approximation-free particle filtering that rigorously fuses observational data with diffusion model simulations for state correction.

problem: Prioritizing protein-protein interactions for experimental validation is challenging because modern deep learning methods produce high false positives despite capturing biological signals.
approach: Introduces PPI candidate ranking framework using interpretability-guided ranking and integrating complementary sources: interaction scores, structural plausibility, biomedical language features.
contribution: Achieves significant improvements over state-of-the-art PPI prediction models on large-scale dataset from successive STRING releases.

problem: Solving geometric problems requires interleaved plot-reasoning steps, but supervised fine-tuning on such data degrades reasoning performance compared to text-only baselines.
approach: Faire uses reinforcement learning to enforce three causal constraints ensuring functional alignment where plotting is internalized rather than superficially imitated.
contribution: Induces qualitative shift in model behavior achieving competitive performance on challenging geometric reasoning benchmarks.

problem: Transformers lack inductive biases for geometric symmetries common in science and vision, and existing equivariant methods sacrifice efficiency.
approach: Platonic Transformer defines attention relative to Platonic solid symmetry group reference frames, inducing weight-sharing for combined equivariance without additional cost.
contribution: Achieves competitive performance on CIFAR-10, 3D point clouds, and molecular benchmarks while maintaining standard transformer efficiency.

problem: Probabilistic models trained with task-agnostic objectives like log-loss lead to significant errors in downstream estimation, especially propensity scores near extremes.
approach: Derives task-specific strictly proper scoring rules by matching local curvature of downstream error metric, applied to Average Treatment Effect estimation.
contribution: Tailored objective consistently outperforms standard likelihood-based and covariate-balancing approaches on causal inference benchmarks.

problem: Attention score overflow risk in low-precision training is underestimated because existing bounds ignore the rank structure of the interaction matrix.
approach: Derives rank-aware concentration inequality showing tail probabilities decay as exp(-d^2α^2/(γr)) when interaction matrix has rank r, yielding geometry-aware scale factors.
contribution: Achieves 8-28x tighter concentration bounds; eliminates overflows in FP8 training across GPT-2 XL to Llama-2-70B while maintaining accuracy.

problem: Momentum SGD relies on fixed momentum coefficient across all parameters, failing to account for heterogeneous loss landscape structure.
approach: Introduces adaptive momentum coefficients regulated by parameter kinetic energy, linking to cubic damping from structural dynamics; augments mSGD and Adam.
contribution: Demonstrates robustness and matches or outperforms Adam on ViT, BERT, and GPT2 training where mSGD typically struggles.

problem: Optimal architectural choices for scaling metagenomic foundation models remain unexplored among autoregressive Transformers, State-Space Models, and long-convolutional architectures.
approach: EDEN studies architectural trade-offs across Llama, Mamba, and Hyena on 28 billion parameter models trained on 9.7 trillion nucleotide tokens.
contribution: Demonstrates Llama architecture exhibits superior scaling efficiency and semantic retrieval; derives quality-aware power-law scaling laws for metagenomics.

problem: Kernel-based conditional conformal prediction provides distribution-free guarantees but suffers from prohibitive computational costs in RKHS-based frameworks.
approach: SpeedCP computes the full solution path of regularized RKHS conformal optimization at essentially single kernel quantile fit cost with simultaneous hyperparameter tuning.
contribution: Provides reliable conditional coverage with 30% improved interval length and 40-fold speedup over Gibbs et al. (2025) across black-box predictors.

problem: Sampling multiple LLM responses to identify consistent answers requires excessive sampling, but optimal stopping leverages Bayesian priors and coarse answer tracking.
approach: Bayesian stopping policy tracks only L=3 most frequent answer counts, proven asymptotically optimal and strictly dominating prior-free baselines.
contribution: Achieves similar answer accuracy using fewer samples by identifying the most consistent LLM answer with fast posterior computation.

problem: Existing neural audio codecs using RVQ, VQ, or FSQ quantization limit geometric structure of latent space, reducing representation learning efficiency.
approach: Q2D2 projects feature pairs onto structured 2D grids (hexagonal, rhombic, rectangular) with implicit codebook defined by grid level products.
contribution: Improves audio compression efficiency with low token rates and high codebook utilization while maintaining state-of-the-art reconstruction quality.

problem: Non-stationary time series forecasting is challenged by fixed expert pools and memoryless routing that fail to adapt to abrupt regime shifts.
approach: Dynamic TMoE detects distribution shifts via Maximum Mean Discrepancy to dynamically instantiate and prune experts, using temporal memory router for context-aware selection.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance across nine benchmarks, reducing MSE by 10.4% and MAE by 7.8%.

problem: On-policy distillation of vision-language models fails to account for orthogonal optimization objectives in language prior and visual grounding.
approach: Visual Gradient Steering (VGS) decomposes loss into language and visual components, then dynamically reorients gradients to prioritize visual subspace.
contribution: Significantly outperforms standard monolithic on-policy distillation with superior grounding and minimal training overhead.

problem: Surrogate regret bounds for online structured prediction break down under non-stationarity where fixed estimators incur linear loss growth.
approach: Combines dynamic regret analysis of online gradient descent with exploit-the-surrogate-gap technique using convolutional Fenchel-Young loss.
contribution: Upper bound depends on F_T and P_T (path length) with tight dependence; Polyak-style learning rate systematically yields target-loss bounds.

problem: Existing AI-generated image detectors exhibit prediction asymmetry (bias toward real class) limiting sensitivity to generated content under post-processing.
approach: DEAR uses inpainted images to identify spurious features by measuring channel activation alignment with inpaint masks, then prunes extreme features.
contribution: Significantly enhances robustness against unseen generators and post-processing operations, mitigating prediction asymmetry.

problem: Prompt learning for missing modalities overlooks internal structural information of prompt vectors, limiting performance under diverse missing modality scenarios.
approach: Structured Prompt Refining (SPR) network refines prompt structure via global interaction fusion, local feature refinement, and channel feature selection modules.
contribution: Uses only 0.8% trainable parameters; surpasses state-of-the-art by 3.8% F1-Macro on MM-IMDB at 90% modality missing rate.

problem: Data-Free Quantization of ViTs suffers from distribution mismatch between synthetic samples and quantized model's expected input due to sparse informative patches.
approach: MaskAQ decouples informative regions from background via differential entropy maximization, selects regions via masked attention alignment, refreshes samples periodically.
contribution: Aligns full-precision models with quantized models while preserving mutual information with synthetic samples across multiple ViT backbones.

problem: Pairwise comparison-based model rankings raise concerns about rewarding superficial cues or displaying judge biases compared to ground-truth accuracy.
approach: Converts five benchmarks into free-form generative evaluations and compares Elo rankings with accuracy rankings using Spearman correlation.
contribution: Elo rankings achieve Spearman correlation above 0.9 with accuracy rankings; style and judge bias have minor effects, echo is a causal driver.

problem: Training diffusion transformers at ultra-high resolutions is extremely costly due to quadratic scaling of self-attention with image tokens.
approach: Dynamic Position Extrapolation (DyPE) adjusts positional encodings at each step to match their frequency spectrum with diffusion process stage.
contribution: Enables pre-trained diffusion transformers to synthesize images at resolutions far beyond training data (e.g., 16 million pixels) without additional sampling cost.
